crime: Every dusk, one prisoner read her sister's last letter at the upper railing. She had sewn it into the lining of her coat so it could never be lost, and she let only {WITCH_NAME} stand beside her. {WITCH_NAME} always came up dressed in plain grey for her.

One cold dusk, the girl wrapped her coat around {WITCH_NAME}. {WITCH_NAME}'s fingers found the letter stitched into the lining. The girl pulled the coat back off her shoulders. "That's mine." Then she turned back to the railing to read alone.

At thirteen, in her father's new house, {WITCH_NAME}'s stepsister had pulled a coat she'd long outgrown off {WITCH_NAME}'s shoulders in the hallway. {WITCH_NAME} had worn it to her first dinner there. "That's mine."
"I wear whatever fits where I am," {WITCH_NAME} used to say. "None of it is mine."

At the railing, she seized the girl by the coat and heaved her over. The collar ripped, and {WITCH_NAME} was left holding the coat. She put it on, pictured it whole, and turned once; it hung whole on her. She took it off and folded it over the railing where the girl had stood.

At lockup, the girl didn't come down. Her roommate found her on the courtyard path below the railing, her sister's letter, torn out of the lining, clenched in her fist. Above, the prisoners found her coat folded over the railing.
In the trial court, the prisoners ruled that she had folded her coat and jumped, holding the letter she had torn out to take with her.
Then her roommate unfolded the coat to sew the letter back in. The lining was whole. There was no hole where the letter had been torn out.

The prisoners understood. A coat with a piece torn from it comes back whole only if {WITCH_NAME} has pictured it that way. The girl hadn't taken off her coat at the railing. She had been pulled out of it.
fields.epitaph: She could make any coat whole, and never learned what anyone kept inside one.
execution: The execution stand raises the coat stand from her father's hallway until it towers as tall as the trial court. Heavy coats hang from its hooks, one for every crowd she ever dressed for. She is strapped to the bench at its foot, beneath a single bare hook that bears her name.
One by one, the hooks tip, and the coats drop onto her. The heap of wool climbs past her shoulders, then over her head.
At last the coat stand looms stripped above the still heap. Only the bare hook with her name is left.

magic.name: Quick Change
magic.text: With a single turn, whatever she's wearing becomes any real outfit she can picture.
